LESSON: WEAVING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Weaving
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Weaving, part of Creating and Executing in Grade 6 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is recycling beneficial to the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. research in virtual and actual sources to identify a plain weave,

2. collect and prepare recyclable materials for weaving such as yarns, fibres among others)

3. make a serrated card loom on a stiff material and a shuttle,

4. weave a mat/scarf using a serrated card loom with emphasis on colour variation,

5. finish the mat/scarf by cutting and tying the tassels,

6. display and positively critique each other’s woven items for reflective feedback,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. research in virtual and actual sources to identify a plain weave,
2. collect and prepare recyclable materials for weaving such as yarns, fibres among others)
3. make a serrated card loom on a stiff material and a shuttle,
4. weave a mat/scarf using a serrated card loom with emphasis on colour variation,
5. finish the mat/scarf by cutting and tying the tassels,
6. display and positively critique each other’s woven items for reflective feedback,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Weaving together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner weaves a mat/scarf using a plain weave on a serrated card loom.

• Learning to learn: The learner acquires new skill to make a mat or scarf using plain weaving technique.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner puts into practise the aspects of safety, care of the environment while sourcing for materials for

weaving.

• Respect: The learner appreciates and appraises others’ woven items using appropriate language.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: The learner observes safety as they prepare a serrated card loom for weaving.

• Climate change: The learner uses materials that are friendly to the environment when improvising the yarns and loom for

weaving.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner measures and cuts to make a serrated card loom.
